Granny's pecan bars

Granny's pecan bars 88

The contrast of toas
ted oats, dark honey, and salted pecans under bitter
chocolate makes these a reliable lunchbox favorite

MAKES ABOUT 24
2509/902/2'% cups rolled
(porridge) oats

cup light
(soft) brown sugar
175g/602/% cup unsalted
butter, softened

For the filling
909/302/7 tbsp unsalted
utter, diced

1 Preheat the oven to 170°C/325°F/Gas 3. Lightly oil

90g/302/% cup dark muscovado
(brown) sugar
1 x 400g/140z can sweetened
condensed milk

For the topping
90g/30z dark (bittersweet)
chocolate

90g/30z toasted pecans
50g/20z pumpkin seeds

a 33 x 23cm/13 x 9in baking tin (quarter sheet pan) and
cover with baking paper.

2 Stir the oats and brown sugar together in a bowl and work in the
butter with your fingertips until the mixture looks like damp sand.
Keep going until it clumps when you squeeze it.

3 Tip the oats into the tin and flatten them firmly
with the base of a glass until the layer is level. Dock
the layer with a fork and bake
for roughly 18 minutes, or until set at the edges and pale
gold. Cool it in the tin.

4 To make the filling, tip the butter, muscovado
sugar and condensed milk into a saucepan and warm slowly,
stirring, until the grains are gone.

5 Bring the pan up to a bubble, stirring without a break.
Turn it down and let it blip quietly, still stirring
the whole time, for about 6-8 minutes, or until it has
darkened and turned thick. Take the
pan off the heat.

6 Scrape the filling over the oat base, level it out,
then leave until firm.

7 To make
the topping, melt the chocolate
gently in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water
or in a microwave in short bursts. Pour it over the set filling
and tilt the tin to spread it.

8 Add small spoonfuls of pecans and seeds. Press them lightly
into the chocolate. Leave until hard,
lift out of the tin, then slice into bars.
